honesty.status: AUTHORED: every lesson, every step order and every sentence in this pack was written here, by us. Nothing is generated, nothing is fetched and no model runs behind any of it. The word AI-SYNTHESIZED belongs to orbis/ and describes generated video; it would be a false label for a hand-written walk through a building.
honesty.content: unverified general practice. These lessons were written to be argued with, corrected and replaced by journey-level practitioners from the halls they name - the same standing the module pack, the recovered stations and the simulator seats already carry, and for the same reason: nobody who does this work for a living has reviewed a line of it yet.
honesty.not_certification: no lesson here certifies anybody, qualifies anybody or permits anybody to do anything. Completing every lesson in this registry would leave a learner with exactly the standing they started with. Where a trade has a real ticket, that ticket is issued by a jurisdiction, an employer or a hall, and this bundle is none of those and speaks for none of them.
honesty.not_a_gate: a lesson unlocks nothing. No step is locked behind another, the ladder is guidance about a sensible order rather than a permission system, and the assessment gate that schools/ declares stays exactly where it is: an unaided verification run that no lesson, station hour or simulator seat substitutes for.
honesty.not_scored: finishing a lesson changes no score and is read by no grader. Four of the eight step kinds write an episode to the existing device-local training log; the other four write nothing at all, and the registry says which is which rather than leaving it to be discovered.
honesty.one_truth: this pack holds no second copy of anything. Hall names, room labels, station names, seat names, scenario names, advisor names, crew role names and topic wordings are all read at build time from the registries that own them, and the test re-reads them the same way. A step that could not resolve its ids did not become a lesson with a footnote; it failed the build.
honesty.no_jurisdiction: nothing here cites a standard, a code or an authority, and nothing here speaks for one. Where a step says what a crew would do, that is unverified general practice and not an instruction from anybody with the standing to give one.
honesty.scope: this is a small set deliberately spread thin: a couple of dozen lessons across a couple of dozen halls, out of 111 halls and 1,221 rooms. It demonstrates the shape a lesson takes in this bundle. It is not a curriculum, it does not cover a trade, and no hall is finished because one of its rooms now has a lesson standing in it.

spread.note: breadth over the trades rather than depth in one: the ceiling is declared, computed and failed against, and all 11 strands must be stood in or the build stops.

walk.act: walk to a room of this hall
walk.why_no_episode: arriving somewhere is not an achievement, and a bundle that logged footsteps would be counting attendance while claiming to teach

placard.act: read the door placard of a room and take on what it requires
placard.why_no_episode: the placard states the room condition record; reading a record changes nothing and is nobody's score

station.act: take a training station at its bench
station.why_no_episode: a station mark lands in the device-local progress record the halls already keep; the training log holds simulator, advisor, crew and walkaround episodes and this pack adds no fifth kind to it

crib.act: run the district crib check at the pegboard
crib.why_no_episode: the crib check is graded deterministically against the crib record and kept with the progress record, not as a training episode

walkaround.act: walk one pre-shift point of a seat and mark it

sim.act: run one seat on the scenario its campus owns

advisor.act: ask the advisor who stands in this room one of its fixed topics

crew.act: ask one role of the standing crew one of its fixed topics while the seat runs

yard.what: the yard the seat is entered from and the crew musters in

plugs_into.loop: explore at home, build and practice in class, verify unaided; the teacher circulates instead of lecturing
plugs_into.how: a lesson is the class and floor halves of the existing loop made walkable, in the order somebody chose. It is not a fifth stage, it does not replace the module pack at home, and it never touches the unaided gate.

painters-contain-it.title: Catch what you wash off
painters-contain-it.why: What comes off a surface has to go somewhere, and the plan for that is either made beforehand or not at all.
painters-contain-it.limits: Finishing this is no environmental permit and no containment design; what may be released, and where, is a jurisdiction matter and this bundle names no jurisdiction.

steps.note: Induction is where containment stops being somebody else problem.
steps.do: Walk to the Induction & PPE — gowning, atmospheric checks, permit board.

steps.note: Read what is in force in the room before you argue about what the job needs.
steps.do: Read the door placard of the Induction & PPE: it states the light, air, noise and protective equipment that room is held to.

steps.note: Where the water goes is a decision, and an undecided one is still a decision.
steps.do: Walk the Pressure Washer Surface Clean seat and mark the point "Work-area containment": drain cover or berm set and the area barricaded before the first spray.

steps.note: Ask what the hazard in this room actually is rather than the one you expected.
steps.do: Ask the Safety steward in the Induction & PPE: "What is the hazard here?"

steps.note: Clean it without damaging it, and watch what the containment number does while you hurry.
steps.do: Run the Pressure Washer Surface Clean seat on the Ferry terminal seawall scenario.

painters-lay-the-coat.title: Lay a coat that is actually there
painters-lay-the-coat.why: A finish fails at the thin places nobody saw, and spraying faster makes more of them rather than fewer.
painters-lay-the-coat.limits: Finishing this coats nothing and is no coating specification; film thickness, recoat windows and compatibility on a real job come from the product data sheet.

steps.note: The practice floor is where overlap becomes a habit instead of an intention.
steps.do: Walk to the Practice Bays — the floor the trade is actually learned on.

steps.note: Atomised coating is a respiratory problem before it is a finish problem.
steps.do: Walk the Airless Paint Sprayer Finish seat and mark the point "Respirator and ventilation": organic-vapor cartridge seated and fit-tested, area ventilated per the coating data sheet.

steps.note: Watch the thin spots and the runs argue with each other; the middle of that argument is the technique.
steps.do: Run the Airless Paint Sprayer Finish seat on the Ferry terminal finish coat scenario.

hazmat-wash-and-decon.title: Come out cleaner than what you washed
hazmat-wash-and-decon.why: The end of a decontamination job is the part where people get exposed, because the hard work is already finished.
hazmat-wash-and-decon.limits: Finishing this is no abatement or decontamination qualification and clears no site; clearance is a measured, sampled process and nothing here samples anything.

steps.note: Gowning and the atmospheric check happen here, in that order, for a reason.
steps.do: Walk to the Induction & PPE — gowning, atmospheric checks, permit board.

steps.note: Read the room record, then read it again for what it does not cover.
steps.do: Read the door placard of the Induction & PPE: it states the light, air, noise and protective equipment that room is held to.

steps.note: What the water can do to a surface it can also do to a hand.
steps.do: Walk the Pressure Washer Surface Clean seat and mark the point "Eye and face protection": safety glasses or face shield seated, no gaps at the seal.

steps.note: Ask what light, air and noise this room is held to, because those numbers are the room promise.
steps.do: Ask the Safety steward in the Induction & PPE: "Light, air and noise?"

steps.note: Run the regional case and notice how much of the score is about what you caught rather than what you cleaned.
steps.do: Run the Pressure Washer Surface Clean seat on the Levee floodwall mildew scenario.

electricians-clip-in-first.title: Clip in before the basket moves
electricians-clip-in-first.why: Nearly everyone who falls from a basket was attached to something for most of the shift.
electricians-clip-in-first.limits: Finishing this is not aerial lift training and is no familiarisation on any machine; a real lift requires machine-specific training and this seat is schematic.

steps.note: The bay is where a machine gets checked out to a training area rather than borrowed.
steps.do: Walk to the Equipment Bay — plant checked out to a training area.

steps.note: An anchor you did not look at is an anchor you are hoping about.
steps.do: Walk the Boom Lift Basket Work seat and mark the point "Harness and anchor point": webbing and stitching whole, lanyard in date, the basket anchor rated and unbent.

steps.note: Ask when the clip goes on, and notice the answer is earlier than you thought.
steps.do: With the seat running, ask the Aerial lift crew's Basket operator: "Why clip to the basket?"

steps.note: Work the points in order and let the envelope warnings teach you the shape of the machine.
steps.do: Run the Boom Lift Basket Work seat on the Curtain-wall panel run scenario.

glaziers-watch-the-line.title: Keep the boom out of the zone
glaziers-watch-the-line.why: Overhead lines do not need to be touched to kill somebody, which is why the observer job exists at all.
glaziers-watch-the-line.limits: Finishing this is no qualified person status and sets no approach distance; approach limits are set by the utility and the jurisdiction, and this bundle sets none.

steps.note: Acceptance criteria and sign-off live here, and an observer is an acceptance job.
steps.do: Walk to the Inspection Bench — acceptance criteria and sign-off.

steps.note: Read the room record before you start deciding what good looks like.
steps.do: Read the door placard of the Inspection Bench: it states the light, air, noise and protective equipment that room is held to.

steps.note: Look up before the machine does, because it will not.
steps.do: Walk the Boom Lift Basket Work seat and mark the point "Overhead-hazard scan": every line, beam and canopy on the run found and its clearance called before the first lift.

steps.note: Ask what the zone is and who is allowed to say it has moved.
steps.do: With the seat running, ask the Aerial lift crew's Line observer: "What is the exclusion zone?"

site-safety-make-it-normal.title: Make stopping the job an ordinary thing to do
site-safety-make-it-normal.why: A culture is measured by how a stop-work call is received, not by how the poster is worded.
site-safety-make-it-normal.limits: Finishing this is no safety qualification and confers no authority on a site; the only authority a stop-work call has is the one the employer and the jurisdiction actually give it.

steps.note: Level tests and the instructor track live here, which is where culture gets taught or not.
steps.do: Walk to the Classroom — level tests and the instructor track.

steps.note: Work the bench and treat the doctrine line as the sentence you will have to say in front of people.
steps.do: Take the Jobsite Safety Culture station at the Classroom bench.

steps.note: Ask what a gate actually is here, and what it refuses to count.
steps.do: Ask the Foreman in the Briefing Room: "Is the walkaround a gate?"

surveyors-trust-the-control.title: Work from control, not from something near it
surveyors-trust-the-control.why: Every layout error that survives to the end of a job started by trusting a mark that was never control.
surveyors-trust-the-control.limits: Finishing this establishes no control network and checks no instrument; a real network is observed, adjusted and recorded, and nothing here does any of those.

steps.note: Setting out lives here, which makes this the right room to be pedantic in.
steps.do: Walk to the Layout Floor — setting out, control points, marking.

steps.note: Read the room record; light matters to this work more than people expect.
steps.do: Read the door placard of the Layout Floor: it states the light, air, noise and protective equipment that room is held to.

steps.note: Ask what control is, then ask how you would know if it had moved.
steps.do: Ask the Layout hand in the Layout Floor: "What is a control point?"

steps.note: Ask what the check is, because a layout without one is a guess with a decimal point.
steps.do: Ask the Layout hand in the Layout Floor: "How do I know the line is true?"
names_read: How do I know the line is true?

steps.note: Five picks against the district record, which is a fair test of whether you know the kit by name.
steps.do: Run the Crib check at the Survey, safety & environment tool crib pegboard — 5 picks.

line-workers-find-the-fault.title: Find the fault instead of replacing things
line-workers-find-the-fault.why: Swapping parts until it works is not diagnosis, it is spending somebody else money in a hopeful order.
line-workers-find-the-fault.limits: Finishing this diagnoses nothing and authorises no switching; live distribution work is governed by the utility own procedures and this bundle holds none of them.

steps.note: Fault-finding against live rigs has its own room because it needs a different head to the practice floor.
steps.do: Walk to the Diagnostic Bench — fault-finding against live rigs.

steps.note: Read what the room is held to before you start pulling at anything.
steps.do: Read the door placard of the Diagnostic Bench: it states the light, air, noise and protective equipment that room is held to.

steps.note: Five picks against the district record; diagnosis starts with knowing what you are holding.
steps.do: Run the Crib check at the Energy & utilities tool crib pegboard — 5 picks.

steps.note: Walk the finding to where acceptance is decided, because a diagnosis nobody accepts is a rumour.
steps.do: Walk to the Inspection Bench — acceptance criteria and sign-off.

steps.note: Ask what is scored and what is not, and listen for how narrow the answer is.
steps.do: Ask the Inspector in the Inspection Bench: "Can I talk my way to a pass?"
names_read: Can I talk my way to a pass?

hvacr-prove-the-sequence.title: Prove the system does what the sequence says
hvacr-prove-the-sequence.why: Commissioning is the moment somebody finds out whether the building does what the drawings promised.
hvacr-prove-the-sequence.limits: Finishing this commissions nothing and signs off nothing; a real commissioning record is witnessed and measured, and no measurement here left this browser.

steps.note: Acceptance criteria live here, and commissioning is acceptance with instruments attached.
steps.do: Walk to the Inspection Bench — acceptance criteria and sign-off.

steps.note: Read the room record, including the part about noise.
steps.do: Read the door placard of the Inspection Bench: it states the light, air, noise and protective equipment that room is held to.

steps.note: Ask whether a good explanation can stand in for a measurement, and note how short the answer is.
steps.do: Ask the Inspector in the Inspection Bench: "Can I talk my way to a pass?"
names_read: Can I talk my way to a pass?

steps.note: Five picks against the district record; the kit is half the argument in this trade.
steps.do: Run the Crib check at the Building-systems tool crib pegboard — 5 picks.

fiber-splicers-keep-the-trace.title: Keep the trace that proves the splice
fiber-splicers-keep-the-trace.why: A splice nobody recorded is a splice somebody will have to find again in the dark.
fiber-splicers-keep-the-trace.limits: Finishing this splices nothing and certifies no link; a real loss budget is measured against a standard and this bundle names and speaks for no standard.

steps.note: As-builts live here, and an as-built is the only proof a buried route ever gets.
steps.do: Walk to the Records — permits, certificates, as-builts.

steps.note: Read the room record; this is a clean room in spirit even when it is not one on paper.
steps.do: Read the door placard of the Records: it states the light, air, noise and protective equipment that room is held to.

steps.note: Ask where the record goes and who is able to read it after you have gone.
steps.do: Ask the Records clerk in the Records: "Where does my progress go?"

steps.note: Ask plainly whether anything here is a certificate, and take the answer seriously.
steps.do: Ask the Records clerk in the Records: "What does the Academy certify?"

carpenters-return-it-the-same.title: Return it in the state you would want to find it
carpenters-return-it-the-same.why: Crib discipline is not tidiness, it is the next person being able to start work without a search.
carpenters-return-it-the-same.limits: Finishing this is no tool competency and is no inventory of any real toolroom; no manufacturer or brand is named here and none is endorsed.

steps.note: Issue, calibration and return are one loop and this room is the whole loop.
steps.do: Walk to the Tool Crib — issue, calibration and return.

steps.note: Read what the room is held to; calibration cares about conditions.
steps.do: Read the door placard of the Tool Crib: it states the light, air, noise and protective equipment that room is held to.

steps.note: Ask what is actually issued here, which is a shorter list than most people expect.
steps.do: Ask the Crib keeper in the Tool Crib: "What is issued out of this crib?"
names_read: What is issued out of this crib?

steps.note: Five picks against the district record, scored deterministically and with nothing narrative able to change it.
steps.do: Run the Crib check at the Envelope & finish tool crib pegboard — 5 picks.

ladder.enforcement: none. The ladder is a sensible order, not a permission system: no lesson is locked behind another and the page contract forbids the page from locking one.

page_contract.data: ship this registry to the page as D.lessons, the same way D.guide and D.crews already arrive: the whole document, indexed by lesson id, with no per-lesson preprocessing. The page adds no field to it at boot.
page_contract.hall: in the hall view, a hall that any lesson names gets one chip per lesson on the hall roster, reading the lesson title and the room label of its strand. The chip is a way in, not a gate: it grants nothing and hides nothing.
page_contract.room: inside the hall the page already tracks curRoom and knows curRoom.strand. When the strand of the room the learner has walked into matches a lesson standing in that hall, the lesson becomes the active one; when they walk out, it stops being active. No other state is kept.
page_contract.hud: while a lesson is active the hfocus line keeps the room label and finish it already shows, and the hint line shows the lesson title, the current step number out of the step count, and that step's computed `do` line - never the note, which is commentary for a reader rather than an instruction for a learner mid-room.
page_contract.reads: the page must READ and never copy: the room label from the strand, the station name from D.stations, the seat name, scenario name and walkaround point from D.sims, the advisor and crew role names and the exact topic wording from D.advisors and D.crews, and the condition line for a placard step from the same condOf()/condLine() pair the hint line already uses. This registry stores ids for all of those on purpose.
page_contract.steps: render the steps in the order given, numbered. A step is marked done by the learner, in this browser only. A step is never enforced: the page must let somebody do step four first, because the building does, and a lesson that could trap a learner in a room would be a gate wearing a lesson's clothes.
page_contract.records: a step whose `records` is a string writes exactly that episode kind through the training recorder that already exists, with no new field and no new storage key. A step whose `records` is null writes nothing - the page must not invent an episode for it, and must not mark the lesson as recorded because a learner walked somewhere.
page_contract.ladder: render a lesson's prerequisites as named links with the edge reason shown. Do not disable a lesson whose prerequisites are unfinished: the ladder is advice about order and the registry says so, and enforcing it in the page would turn it into the gate this pack promises it is not.
page_contract.limits: the `limits` sentence renders with the lesson, not behind a disclosure control, and not only at the end. A learner who is told what a lesson does not mean only after finishing it has already formed the belief the sentence exists to prevent.
page_contract.episode: nothing about opening, reading or abandoning a lesson is recorded. The only episodes that reach the training log are the four the step kinds already declare, written by the recorder that was already writing them.
